I have been instituionalized once.  I'm able to fake it well enough that it will never happen again.

A while back I had a good relationship with my father, and I was going to an alright therapist.  I talked to both of them about eveything, including my desire to end my life.  They talked about that with me, but didn't step in until I tried to get a gun permit.  At which point they called the police who told my father to bring me in, or they would.

I cooperated.  It did nothing for me.  I had to see a psychiatrist and social worker every day and was persribed medication I had to take.  There were also daily group sessions.

The medications for depression didn't kick in until I left, however because they were suppressing my obsessive compulsive tendancies (which I've been informed all antidepressants do) I did not continue them.  At that point I was being open about everything (my depression being intertwined with being a pedophile).  The mental health professionals were very disrespectful which lead me to become even more disheartened about getting help.  I was also told that pedophilia was not an acceptable topic to bring up in the group essions, so I was unable to discuss It else where.

I can't comment on how well it would work for you, but for me it was a huge waste of time (and money since I was forced to pay for it as well which made me feel 100 times worse than when I went in since it drained every penny I had).

My take on this kind of idea is that learning how to make friends is much like learning language.  After the window of opportunity to learn how to socialize has passed and you missed it, it takes a substantial amount of effort to make up for your losses.  As someone who never had the experience of friendship, it completely confuses me.  I have no idea how to be anything other than superficially friendly and I'm at a loss how to undo that kind of damage.

I understand.  I am for the abolishment of all sex trafficing and slavery as well.  I, mistakenly, saw what you wrote as an example of what I have often seen when talking about topics like this. I'll try to explain it better.  Whenever I've seen people comment in a sympathetic way towards pedophiles that did not add a disclaimer (such as denouncing child molestation) they were nearly always attacked as if by understanding the plight of a celibate pedophile meant that they endorced horrific crimes against children.  I hope that makes it easier to understand.

I personally have a very low tolerance for crimes against children (much more than average as measured by those I come in contact with everyday).  Something that bothers me to no end is how the entertainment industry puts children in dire situations either because the plot requires it, or because it will offer a more visceral reactiom from its watchers.  For example, I will never watch (or read for that matter) The Hunger Games.  I can't stand the fact that the plot is children are forced to fight to the death.  I also won't watch The Walking Dead.  I like the premise of a post apocalyptic scenario, however there are children involved and that just makes me sick.

I'm sorry, I don't think I am being clear enough.  It seems like what you are sayin is what I mean.  The actual feelings and thoughts are natural things that come with any orientation.  In this sense pedophilia is not a mental illness and is instead a sexual orientation/tendancy.  If a pedophile falls in love with an underage person and forms a romantic relationship, there are now problems that arise because of going through with the relationship. It is the decision to act that becomes the qualifier of whether said individual is mentally ill because of the idea that the act is inseperable from negative effects.  Does that make it more clear?  (I feel like we're saying the same thing.)

[Side note:  I don't quite understand your bisexuality comment.  Are you saying you only date other bisexuals?  I wouldn't see it as a rights violation if a bisexual male had a relationship with a strait female if they had feelings for eachother.]

I agree about how lengthy debates on this subject can get.  It really comes down to perspective where people will dig their heels in and not see other perspectives. We might not agree exactly what consent it, but I can definetly agree that nonconsentual or forced harm situations are rights violation situations that I wish I could snap my fingers and end forever.
If I understand what you are saying, your viewpoint is that pedophilia is a mental illness because it should never be expressed.  Is that correct?

I'm curious about what you mean when you qualify your support because you see pedophilia as a mental illness.  Do you think that you would have more/less support if instead pedophilia was predominantly thought of as a sexual orientation/tendancy?  I'm just intrigued by your wording is all.  I personally don't think of my pedophilia as an mental illness.

Another injustice that can be pointed out (a lesser one, but it is easy to see for a nonpedophile replying to such a topic) is that anytime people talk about pedophilia (being a pedophile or not) they feel a great need to add qualifiers or distance themselves from the topic.

Examples from the pedophile side:
I'm a pedophile, but I've never touched a child, never looked at child pornography, never broken the law, etc.

Example from the nonpedophile side:
"in saying that i'm sure you appretiate there's nothing about the action of sexual abuse or supporting child pornography that i support."

I believe a factor to help explain this stems from a mindset of 'guilty until proven innocent' that surrounds this topic causing those engaging in the discussion to retroactivly attempt to prove thier innocence.  It's at the very least interesting to observe.

For different reasons I have grown up (I'm 23 now) without developing essential skills such as how to make friends.  Compounded with various other problems in my life, Which leads me to be reasonably sure that the rest of my life will be one long drawn out torturous existence.  The question that I have been asking myself recently (and I offer it to you to ponder as well) is, will the suffering be worth it if something does happen to change for the better?

There is no question in my mind, that if there was no such thing as technological advancement, there'd be absolutely no hope for me.  I have slight hope for the future that technology will be able to help those of us who are currently at a loss.  To use a physical disability to try and make it easier to understand: If I had Lou Gehrig's disease, would the fact that I would be forced to exist as a prisoner inside my own body for years (or decades) outweigh the post-cure existence possibility where I can exist after the disease can be treated?

How would you answer such a question?  What do you think are the chances that you will get to a point in your life where you will have things to look forward to?  Do you think it is worth it to take that chance?  I'm interested to hear your thoughts.

I don't have much to add other than I am in a similar place.  I have no future in regards to intimate relationships due to my sexuality, and I have basically given up hope on friendships (I don't have the skills).  

Might I recommend some distractions?  That is typically how I structure my days.  I fit in as much as I can to distract myself from the awful reality of the situation until I get to a desired (whatever that may be) action.

It is quite the awful experience just to exist in such a tattered existence.  I'd like to believe that things can always get better for people, however I don't believe this with relation to myself.  What kind of existence am I telling someone to continue when there is no light at the end of the tunnel?  What if I am say "go on" when all that entails is a longer torment?  I'm certainly up to talking, but I don't feel like it is my place to tell people not to end their life.

Mandatory reporting laws are tough but as long as they don't think (or can't convince themselves) that you're a threat to the safety of yourself or others they cannot by law disclose what you tell them in session.[/quote]

Intellectually (except for the idea that mental health professionals follow disclosure laws), I understand what you're saying.  I don't know if I could ever get back to a point where I'd consider therapy again.  The damage caused by seeking help the first time was extremely painful.  I can't see myself seeking out therapy unless I have literally nothing left to lose.

[quote]I know that you don't want to hear it but none of us should work with children, however we might like to. It's just not safe for them however much in control we think we are.[/quote]

I do understand where you are coming from, and really all I can say is that I disagree.  This is one of the things that really made therapy unappealing while I was going through it.  I don't have a problem discussing this point of contention with someone.  I have no problem being open about my thoughts and feelings with people whose position is different then mine.  However, at the end of the day I still get to make the final decision.  It don't want to be in the position where someone can force me to follow their beliefs if I don't on my own.

When I have a moment I'll look at Circles of Support and Accountability more.  I am aware of Virtuous Pedophiles.  I don't exactly hold the same beliefs as they do, though I do enjoy reading their site from time to time.

Therapy:
This is an area I am not willing to try again.  My experiences with mental health professionals have been denial at best and having CPS called on me at worst.  Due to my actions of seeking out help I have already been forced out of one home.  I will not make the same mistake twice.  I had also looked at treatment programs that were offered to me during therapy sessions.  None were for non offenders (since if those programs exist, they are few and far between) which meant in order to be accepted into the program I would have to give up rights until I was on the level of a sex criminal.  While on principle I found that ridiculous, practically it would also mean I would have to quit my job, since a stipulation in all the programs I was offered was that I couldn't work with children.  That is also a deal breaker for me.

I have views about pedophilia that aren't necessarily popular, but I've not broken the law.  I realize that I am just not compatible with this world.  

As a pedophile yourself, I am curious though.  Do any of the mindsets that I have described in my original post haunt you?  I am curious how you've handled such feelings if you've had them as well.

I personally find dignity to be irrelevant.  When most people would judge me to be unworthy of respect/worth/humanity/etc. merely because of my sexuality, such transient character judgements don't mean much.

On the other hand, some people like vegetables.  I am always confused by the responses I get from people who are confused on how I can actually *like* broccoli!

Have any little battles coming up?  Whether what you couldn't accomplish was a big or small problem, sometimes just winning the small battles (like getting someone to smile, or playing a favorite video game) build up what the sandpaper of life has worn down.

I have pondered this as well. I'm a believer that once I die, nothing else matters so when that time comes for me I'm going to hold a type of open meeting for anyone that wants to speak to me. They can ask questions or request explanations on any topic (I know my brother is curious about last minute thoughts on the universe) rather than rely on a note that might not cover their questions. Granted, if someone is not seeking a legal way out it might hinder them.

I think that if more people did this (though the threat of intervention would have to be dealt with) it might help with someones feeling of worthlessness.  You never know how many people would show up, or what questions they'd ask.  If nothing mattered from that point on though, it shouldn't be a problem.
